## 📝 Understanding This Market Report

📊 **What is the HPI?**  
The California Housing Price Index (HPI) reflects how home prices have changed over time. Each data point shows the average home price trend for that year across California.  

📈 **Rising prices = Stronger market.**  
An increasing HPI typically means homes are appreciating in value, demand is strong, and sellers have leverage.  

📉 **Falling prices = Cooling market.**  
When the HPI declines, it may reflect market corrections, rising interest rates, or changing buyer behavior.

🗺 **How does this help you?**  
Even though this data reflects state-level averages, Rancho Cucamonga often follows similar trends. Understanding these shifts can help you plan your buying or selling strategy more effectively.

## 📊 Price Trend Chart

```{r}
# ---- Setup ----
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(scales)
  library(lubridate)
  library(tidyr)
})

csv_path <- "data/CAHPI.csv"

if (!file.exists(csv_path)) {
  cat("❗ **Data file not found:** `data/CAHPI.csv`\n\n",
      "• Make sure the file is in the `data/` folder of your project.\n",
      "• Expected columns include a `Date` column plus region HPI columns like:\n",
      "  `CASTHPI`, `San Francisco HPI`, `San Diego HPI`, `Los Angeles HPI`.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  hpi_data <- read_csv(csv_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

  # Try to locate columns by flexible name matching
  find_col <- function(patterns, nm = names(hpi_data)) {
    idx <- lapply(patterns, function(p) grep(p, nm, ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE))
    unique(unlist(idx))[1]
  }

  # Core columns (flexible matching for various header spellings)
  date_col <- find_col(c("^date$"))
  ca_col   <- find_col(c("^casthpi$", "california.*hpi", "^ca.*hpi$"))
  sf_col   <- find_col(c("san\\s*francisco.*hpi", "^sf.*hpi$"))
  sd_col   <- find_col(c("san\\s*diego.*hpi", "^sd.*hpi$"))
  la_col   <- find_col(c("los\\s*angeles.*hpi", "^la.*hpi$"))

  # Minimal required: Date + CA
  if (is.na(date_col) || is.na(ca_col)) {
    cat("❗ **Required columns missing.**\n\n",
        "• I need at least a `Date` column and a California HPI column (e.g., `CASTHPI`).\n",
        "• Found columns: ", paste(names(hpi_data), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    # Parse date
    hpi_data[[date_col]] <- suppressWarnings(mdy(hpi_data[[date_col]]))
    if (all(is.na(hpi_data[[date_col]]))) {
      # Fallback: try ymd
      hpi_data[[date_col]] <- suppressWarnings(ymd(hpi_data[[date_col]]))
    }

    # Build a list of regions that exist
    region_map <- list(
      CA = ca_col,
      SF = sf_col,
      SD = sd_col,
      LA = la_col
    )
    region_map <- region_map[!vapply(region_map, is.na, logical(1))]

    # Yearly averages
    hpi_yearly <- hpi_data %>%
      mutate(Year = year(.data[[date_col]])) %>%
      filter(!is.na(Year)) %>%
      {
        # summarize dynamically based on available regions
        summarise_args <- c(list(Year = quote(Year)), lapply(region_map, function(col) {
          rlang::expr(mean(.data[[!!col]], na.rm = TRUE))
        }))
        group_by(., Year) %>% dplyr::summarise(!!!summarise_args)
      } %>%
      arrange(Year)

    # Pivot to long
    hpi_long <- hpi_yearly %>%
      pivot_longer(cols = -Year, names_to = "Region", values_to = "HPI")

    # Plot
    ggplot(hpi_long, aes(x = Year, y = HPI, group = Region, color = Region)) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
      geom_point(size = 2) +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = pretty(hpi_long$Year, n = 10)) +
      labs(
        title = "California & Regional Housing Price Index (HPI)",
        subtitle = "Annual Averages",
        x = "Year", y = "HPI Index",
        caption = "Source: CA HPI Data"
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.title = element_blank(),
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 9)
      )
  }
}

```
